distractors.reason: 'Do' is used with tasks such as do homework or do the dishes. We don't say 'do a campaign'.
'Take' is used with breaks, photos or actions such as take a look. We don't say 'take a campaign'.
'Get' means receive or obtain. We don't say 'get a campaign' to mean starting a marketing action.

example_sentence: The company will ___ a new campaign next month.
l1_interference: Falantes de português podem traduzir 'lançar' de forma literal e usar 'throw' ou 'do' em inglês. A combinação correta em inglês é 'launch a campaign'.
explanation: In English, 'launch' is the usual verb for starting a campaign, product or advertisement. It means to begin something officially and publicly.

related_collocations.example: They decided to run an ad during the football match.
The video helped us reach a larger audience.
Please pay attention to the advertisement.

memory_tip: LAUNCH = start something public (campaign, product, app) | DO = perform a task (homework, work) | TAKE = action or break (photo, break)
